# Improving the Fairness of ML Pipelines Generated by LLM Agents

We evaluate [AIDE-ML](https://github.com/WecoAI/aideml), an AI agent that automatically generates ML pipelines, focusing on fairness. Across 10 use cases we test how well AIDE produces fair pipelines when prompted for fairness, and compare its outputs against manually crafted alternatives.

## Use Cases

| # | Use Case | Dataset | Sensitive Attributes | Folder |
|---|----------|---------|---------------------|--------|
| 1 | Income Prediction | ACS Income CA ([Folktables](https://github.com/zykls/folktables)) | Race | [`use-cases/income/`](use-cases/income/) |
| 2 | Student Admission | Synthetic (12k applications) | Race, Gender, SES, First-gen | [`use-cases/student-admission/`](use-cases/student-admission/) |
| 3 | Image Generation Stereotypes | ViSAGe + Stable Diffusion v1.5 | Nationality | [`use-cases/image-generation-stereotypes/`](use-cases/image-generation-stereotypes/) |
| 4 | Hiring | ACSEmployment ([Folktables](https://github.com/zykls/folktables)) | Race, Sex | [`use-cases/hiring/`](use-cases/hiring/) |
| 5 | Healthcare Admission | ACSPublicCoverage ([Folktables](https://github.com/zykls/folktables)) | Race, Sex | [`use-cases/healthcare/`](use-cases/healthcare/) |
| 6 | Housing Approval | ACSMobility ([Folktables](https://github.com/zykls/folktables)) | Race, Sex | [`use-cases/housing/`](use-cases/housing/) |
| 7 | Banking Bias | Kaggle credit scoring | Gender | [`use-cases/bank-bias/`](use-cases/bank-bias/) |
| 8 | Crime Prediction | Kaggle multi-class crime | Gender | [`use-cases/crime/`](use-cases/crime/) |
| 9 | Facial Recognition | FairFace (HuggingFace) | Race | [`use-cases/facial/`](use-cases/facial/) |
| 10 | Image Generation for Professions | HuggingFace | Source / Style | [`use-cases/image-generation-for-professions/`](use-cases/image-generation-for-professions/) |

Each use-case folder contains notebooks, results, and (where available) an `overview.md` with detailed methodology and findings.

## Methodology

Although approaches vary with different use cases the general workflow looks something like this:

1. **Baseline with AIDE** — generate a pipeline prompted for accuracy only, with no fairness considerations.
2. **Fairness-prompted AIDE models** — re-run AIDE with prompts that request fairness (varying in specificity).
3. **Alternative approaches** — apply established fairness techniques (e.g., Fairlearn's ThresholdOptimizer, ExponentiatedGradient, reweighting) without AIDE.
4. **Model from scratch** — build a custom fair model (e.g., adversarial debiasing neural networks).
5. **Evaluation & comparison** — measure accuracy alongside fairness metrics (Demographic Parity, Equal Opportunity, CLIP stereotype scores, etc.).
6. **Visualizations & report** — summarise findings for each use case.

The exact techniques and fairness metrics vary per use case depending on the task type and dataset. See the individual use-case folders for details.

## Getting Started

See [`GETTING_STARTED.md`](GETTING_STARTED.md) for setup instructions, dependency installation, and how to explore or reproduce experiments.

> **Note:** Running AIDE experiments requires an API key for the underlying LLM. Exploring pre-computed results does not.

## Key Dependencies

- [AIDE-ML](https://github.com/WecoAI/aideml) — the LLM agent under evaluation
- [Fairlearn](https://fairlearn.org/) — fairness metrics and mitigation algorithms
- [Folktables](https://github.com/zykls/folktables) — US Census ACS datasets (used for some of the datasets)

Full list in [`requirements.txt`](requirements.txt).
